gaps.sentence: "Would you like a drink?" — He ___ me a drink.
'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
gaps.explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said. He ___ shouting at me.
gaps.explanation: Apologies take apologise for + -ing: apologised for shouting.

gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'Thank you for delivering it so quickly,' she said. She ___ me for delivering it so quickly.
gaps.explanation: Thanks are reported as thank somebody for + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.
